evidence_updates.claim: BNY says its Digital Asset Custody platform now supports XRP and RLUSD. BNY/Ripple also intend future direct RLUSD mint/redemption through BNY and are exploring tokenized trade finance/supply-chain finance with C2FO; future plans remain subject to approvals.
evidence_updates.inference: This expands institutional custody and potential settlement/collateral infrastructure around Ripple/XRPL. It does not establish BNY clients' net XRP purchases, realized collateral usage, or price impact.
evidence_updates.disconfirming_or_unknown: Client uptake, custody balances, transaction volume, collateral eligibility, launch timing and marginal XRP demand are not disclosed in this release.

evidence_updates.claim: Circle reported Q2 2026 USDC circulation of $73.3B and on-chain transaction volume of $14.8T; revenue and reserve income totaled $701.3M, including $667.7M reserve income. Circle's H1 filing says distribution costs paid to Coinbase increased $19.8M, reflecting increased reserve income partly offset by Coinbase's lower share of average USDC on-platform balances. Coinbase's Q2 filing reports an all-time high in average USDC held in its products and says it sold a portion of its Circle investment in Q1 2026.
evidence_updates.interpretation: Coinbase-Circle incentives are operational and financial, not merely a loose ecosystem association; the relationship can change over time through distribution economics and equity exposure. These metrics concern USDC and Coinbase/Circle economics, not proof of XRP price support or net XRP accumulation.
evidence_updates.limits: Issuer volume can include repeated transfers, trading, arbitrage and settlement. Coinbase's Q2 filing does not establish its current net XRP position.

market_observations.interpretation: Positive funding and high Binance account-long skew coexist with rising aggregate open interest and larger reported short than long liquidations. This is a mixed positioning snapshot, not a directional signal.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: New institutional custody support can lower operational barriers and expand the feasible set of XRP/RLUSD use cases, but price impact requires evidence of incremental XRP holdings, collateral acceptance, market-maker inventory changes or spot demand.
counter_hypotheses: Custody is safekeeping infrastructure; clients may hold zero XRP or use stablecoins/tokenized receivables instead.
Future RLUSD mint/redeem and C2FO trade-finance work is conditional and may not launch or may not require XRP.
competing_hypotheses.test_plan: Track later BNY disclosures, custody balance/volume metrics if public, actual XRPL transfer and exchange flows, collateral schedules and dated product-launch evidence; compare event windows with matched crypto assets and macro controls.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: Positive funding and elevated Binance account-long skew may indicate crowded long exposure, while the reported greater short-liquidation amount could indicate recent short covering; the combination is insufficient to infer next-period direction.
counter_hypotheses: Aggregate open interest may include hedged positions; account ratios do not measure notional exposure; vendor venue coverage and liquidation feeds may be incomplete.
competing_hypotheses.test_plan: Obtain synchronized exchange-level OI, funding, basis, depth, liquidations, spot volume and price returns; estimate event-time and walk-forward predictive value against a simple market-beta baseline.

forecast_status.reason: Single third-party derivatives snapshot is not independently corroborated; no synchronized multi-venue feature store or validated fixed-horizon model performance is available. BNY announcement and stablecoin metrics do not imply a price target.
